subject.title: refactor(protocol): pre-publish cheat-window cleanup and vintage tracking

question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed breaking cleanup of beta-only gateway-protocol and generated-client surfaces before the package is published publicly?
rationale: The branch intentionally removes and reshapes broad protocol APIs; source evidence alone cannot decide whether the stated unshipped/beta compatibility window is the repository’s intended public-contract boundary.

options.title: Accept the pre-publication cleanup
options.body: Approve the breaking cleanup after conflicts are resolved, the exact package/release audit is reconfirmed, and runtime proof is attached.

options.title: Preserve beta compatibility temporarily
options.body: Retain deprecated aliases or validators for the affected beta surfaces and schedule their removal with an explicit release boundary.

options.title: Split the public-contract decisions
options.body: Land only the non-breaking metadata and internal cleanup, leaving wire-shape and export removals for a narrower protocol decision.

recommendation.title: Accept the pre-publication cleanup
recommendation.body: Approve the breaking cleanup after conflicts are resolved, the exact package/release audit is reconfirmed, and runtime proof is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: Assigned change owner and author of the staged protocol compatibility audit.
